Input 1 is the EDIT TARGET and absolute camera/geometry reference. Inputs 2 and 3 are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: the original kitchen wide and detail photographs. Input 4 is supplementary house style only (dining).
Transform input 1 into a convincing professional interior photograph belonging to exactly the same house as inputs 2–4. Change materials, surface realism, lighting and photographic response only.
GEOMETRY LOCK: preserve input 1's exact perspective, framing, room proportions, every wall edge and opening, broad plaster header, all stair treads, landings, inclined solid stair waist slab and upper return, black balusters/rails, TV size and placement, thin raking backing profile, four low cabinet fronts, low shelf left of TV and two-level open shelf at right. Preserve separate small basin and mirror nook to the right and existing open timber door further right. Preserve the exposed clearance between backing and staircase, circulation and headroom. Do not move or add doors, windows, furniture, stairs or fixtures. Keep original flat-front oak backing, no new fluting or slats.
FINISH: exactly the kitchen's muted natural light oak with restrained fine grain, matte/satin sheen and subtle board variation; remove vivid orange and oversized repeating grain. Warm ivory plaster with delicate texture, pale sandy limestone-look stair and floor surfaces with fine mineral variation and soft reflections; quiet warm greige cabinet fronts. Charcoal-black rail and tap, believable glazed white basin and dark reflective screen. Retain every existing object and its location; just make it physically credible.
LIGHT: soft directional daylight from existing openings, realistic tropical greenery only through the existing window, subtle natural shadow gradients and ambient bounce, balanced neutral-warm exposure. Existing LED positions remain but appear as discreet diffused warm light with controlled highlights, no bright white neon lines or orange glow flooding the room. Match the kitchen photograph's gentle contrast and color grading.
CAMERA: same eye-level wide composition as input 1, architectural photography, straight verticals, crisp natural texture, realistic edge highlights and contact shadows; no plastic smoothness, game-engine look, excessive sharpening, exaggerated marble, sepia filter, decor additions, text or watermark. Single full-frame image.
